frameworks.name: Logic, Evidence, Utility Framework
frameworks.definition: A three-step diagnostic framework for problem definition: state what the problem is (Logic), quantify how you know it (Evidence), and explain why it matters (Utility).

frameworks.name: Demand Unlock Constraint Matrix
frameworks.definition: A four-variable diagnostic for unconstrained growth: messaging clarity, sales motion efficiency, pricing structure, and fast-cash activation capability.

frameworks.name: Qualification Friction Model
frameworks.definition: A framework where increased qualification requirements (good friction) improve ROAS and sales efficiency by filtering away low-intent prospects, enabling smaller closing teams.

frameworks.name: Fast Cash Play Activation
frameworks.definition: An early engagement strategy where existing business resources (past customers, social lists, content) are mobilized in the first 30 days to generate outcome proof and fund the core engagement.

claims.text: Unqualified inbound traffic is typically caused by poor messaging clarity—prospects arrive on the call with no understanding of what the service actually does or how execution works, creating a gap that must be bridged during the sales conversation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business where delivery model is non-obvious

claims.text: For high-traffic inbound scenarios with unqualified prospects, a video sales letter (VSL) serves as a pre-qualification and indoctrination tool before the sales call, filtering low-intent traffic and conditioning decision-making.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Traffic volume sufficient to justify friction addition
Existing sales funnel underperforming on qualification
claims.mechanism: Prospects who encounter VSL are pre-educated on the offer structure and delivery model before commitment, reducing call-time spent on education.

claims.text: Pre-framing through application form design (e.g., a VIP ticket checkbox) increases subsequent purchase likelihood by anchoring prospect expectations before the upsell moment.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: A checkbox signaling VIP interest on the registration form conditions the prospect to self-select into premium positioning, increasing willingness-to-pay downstream.

claims.text: Good friction in sales funnels—qualifying questions, price statements, and high-intent requirements—increases ROAS and sales team efficiency despite raising cost per lead.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales team capacity is constraint, not lead volume
claims.mechanism: Higher qualification requirements filter away low-intent leads, allowing sales reps to focus energy on higher-probability closes, improving conversion rate and extending runway.
bounded_by: Does not apply when lead volume is below sales capacity
Does not apply when entire market is small

claims.text: In B2B service sales with existing demand, most business owners do not allocate untapped resources (dormant customer lists, social media followers, past business contacts) to generate fast cash.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business with 3+ year operating history
Owner has accumulated customer list or social media asset

claims.text: A fast cash campaign mobilizes existing business resources within the first 30 days to generate verifiable client outcomes, allowing business owners to pay for continued engagement using profits from the initial wins.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business with existing delivery capability
Client has some form of reactivatable asset (list, audience, contacts)
claims.mechanism: Immediate proof of concept reduces buyer hesitation and creates self-funding model where initial success funds additional work.
bounded_by: Requires operational bandwidth to execute quickly
May not apply to productized services without customization

claims.text: A core failure in service business onboarding is that advisors deliver a blueprint and build it one-on-one but leave execution to the client, who does not take action despite initial engagement.
claims.speaker: Restaurant Owner (Unnamed)

claims.text: Client action can be incentivized through bonuses, discounts, guarantees contingent on specific actions, and offer structure that ties initial activation outcomes to subsequent service phases.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Contingent incentives (earn discount if you complete X action) create behavioral accountability while preserving intrinsic motivation to execute.

claims.text: Business owners who fail to grow as fast as they'd like are typically misallocating attention and resources, not facing true supply constraints; internal resource reallocation often unlocks undetected growth capacity.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Business owners optimize for comfort (routine activities, known channels) rather than returns; external advisor reallocates the same resources toward higher-ROI activities, producing growth.
bounded_by: Does not apply to businesses with genuinely zero existing resources
Does not apply when demand is actually insufficient

claims.text: The Logic-Evidence-Utility framework requires that problem statements be verifiable: "messaging is off" must be accompanied by evidence (e.g., "80% of calls are unqualified") and a mechanism explaining why the issue matters.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Forcing quantified evidence prevents vague problem statements and surfaces whether the issue is truly binding (a constraint) or symptomatic.

claims.text: When prospects arrive to a sales call unqualified (unfamiliar with the offer), the sales conversation becomes extended education rather than closing, and sales team burden increases significantly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Offer structure is non-obvious or counterintuitive
claims.mechanism: Reps must spend conversation time explaining what the service is and how delivery works, leaving less time for objection handling and closing, reducing conversion.

claims.text: Founder-led operational guarantees—stating facts about what the service delivers and enforcing accountability—are enforceable through clear upfront disclosure and consistent follow-through.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Client success depends on client action
claims.mechanism: Transparency at contract stage sets expectations; consistent enforcement in execution builds trust and reduces service failure disputes.

examples.text: A book launch funnel added a checkbox asking "Do you want a VIP ticket?" to the registration form. The checkbox itself changed nothing about the subsequent page or offer. However, prospects who checked the VIP box were significantly more likely to purchase the VIP tier when presented on the next page, demonstrating that pre-framing alone increased conversion.

An ad campaign for paid traffic acquisition tested two approaches: low friction (broad qualification, cost per call ~$200) vs. high friction (strict qualification including stating price and requiring proof of credibility, cost per call ~$500). Despite doubling the cost per call, the high-friction approach roughly doubled ROAS (3x → 6x) and improved sales team efficiency, allowing the team to close more deals without expanding headcount.

A consulting engagement with a restaurant owner revealed the owner had built a capable operations consulting business ($3.2M revenue on track), but had not mobilized existing resources (past client networks, social media followers, internal contacts) to generate initial outcomes that would fund the next engagement phase. Hormozi diagnosed this as a resource allocation problem, not a demand problem, since the owner already had sufficient demand to reach $10M if resource were reallocated.

practices.text: Use a video sales letter (VSL) or pre-framing content to educate inbound prospects on your offer before they enter the sales conversation, filtering low-intent traffic and reducing the education burden on the sales team.

Implement qualification friction in sales funnels by asking prospects for proof of their stated problem, requiring explicit acknowledgment of price points, and collecting data that surfaces intent; re-test friction levels to find the optimal ROAS point.

In service business onboarding, structure the first 30 days as a fast cash campaign using the client's existing resources (past customer lists, social media, internal contacts) to generate early wins; tie subsequent onboarding phases and discounts to measurable client execution.

Use the Logic-Evidence-Utility framework when diagnosing business problems: define the problem in plain language, provide quantified evidence that it exists, and explain why solving it matters before moving to solution design.

When messaging clarity is low, add a pre-qualification step (VSL, application form) that explains the service delivery model explicitly; measure success by tracking the percentage of qualified vs. unqualified leads attending sales calls.

Enforce client action through contingent incentives: offer discounts, bonuses, or guarantees that unlock only if the client completes specific actions during the onboarding phase; state these conditions upfront and enforce them consistently.
